entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mildest of the blame words, locating blame without characterising the deed, where *guilty* already calls the act reprehensible.

entries.definition: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs the deed and finds it has earned censure, a considered verdict rather than *at fault*'s bare attribution.

entries.definition: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat and formal, stating only that blame may properly be laid, without *blameworthy*'s sense that the deed went out and earned it.

entries.definition: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Equally impersonal, taking the wrong, the evil and the merely injurious alike without changing temperature.

entries.definition: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the blame inside the thing as a quality it is full of, where *blameworthy* says only that blame is deserved.

entries.definition: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pitches the fault toward reproof that could be pronounced out loud, the most public-facing of these.

entries.definition: deserving blame or censure as being wrong or evil or injurious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coolest of these, recording fault as a determination, which is why it sits as easily on the injurious as on the evil.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gravest here - guilt of killing rather than of a misdeed, and the word treats it as a stain carried rather than a charge answered.

entries.definition: liable to be accused, or cause for such liability
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and procedural, recording exposure to accusation and resting as readily on the cause as on the person, so it asserts no wrong.

entries.definition: liable to be accused, or cause for such liability
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weights that same liability toward formal accusation, sounding graver than *chargeable* while claiming no more guilt.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The one inward member, guilt felt from inside rather than laid on from outside, with the conscience itself doing the striking.

entries.definition: guilty of crime or serious offense
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hard and total, making the wrongdoing a category the person belongs to, and it reaches past crime proper to any serious offense.
examples: criminal in the sight of God and man

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Lighter than *criminal* by the size of the deed, chiding a misdeed rather than condemning a crime.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely procedural, measuring the offence as money owed and judging the offender not at all.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: As bloodless as *finable* - a penalty attaches, and nothing is said about the wrong or the wrongdoer.

entries.definition: extended meanings; especially of psychological coldness; without human warmth or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat, unfigured term for the whole condition, naming the missing human warmth without deciding whether it is a settled nature or a rebuff aimed at someone.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Near-clinical: it reports feeling as simply absent from the person, with none of the unfriendliness *icy* points at a target.
examples: he kept his emotionless objectivity and faith in the cause he served

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Where *emotionless* records no feeling at all, this faults a missing ardour, the flatness of something that ought to have had fire in it.
examples: this passionless girl was like an icicle in the sunshine
